claims.claim: Won the 2026 Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium on Monday 26 October; first Englishman in about 25 years
claims.note: UEFA gives the London Palladium Theatre and Monday 26 October; Sky says first English winner in 25 years.

claims.claim: Bayern's fourth Ballon d'Or winner after Beckenbauer, Muller and Rummenigge
claims.note: FOX/AP names the same three players and calls Kane the fourth.

claims.claim: Born 28 July 1993, so 33 years old
claims.note: Wikidata gives 28 July 1993; Khel Now calls him 33-year-old.

claims.claim: Ceremony began 45 minutes late because of London traffic
claims.note: Sky: delayed by 45 minutes to an 8.45pm start due to London traffic.

claims.claim: Vote by 100 journalists; Kane ahead of Mbappe and Yamal; also Striker of the Year
claims.note: Bundesliga 27 Oct: vote by 100 journalists from the top 100 FIFA-ranked nations; placings; Striker of the Year.

claims.claim: Travelled London to Munich for Tuesday training, per Aaron Danks; Bayern teased a special welcome
claims.note: FOX: Danks said Kane was travelling to training on Tuesday; Bayern teased a special welcome.

claims.claim: Danks said Kane would be available to play against Magdeburg
claims.note: FOX: Danks said Kane would be available to play in Wednesday's cup match.

claims.claim: Bayern beat 1. FC Magdeburg 6-1 in the German Cup on Wednesday 28 October; Michael Olise scored twice
claims.note: Sportschau: 6:1 on 28 October; Olise at 10 and 50 minutes.

claims.claim: Kane did not play; rested as a reward for being named Ballon d'Or winner
claims.note: Sportschau: Kane was rested as a reward; he was not on the pitch.

claims.claim: Bayern promised to recognise the award before the Dortmund match on Saturday 31 October; FOX report published before the match
claims.note: FOX: promised recognition of his achievement before the Klassiker; article published before the match.

claims.claim: World Soccer Talk, citing Sky Sports Germany's Florian Plettenberg: extension to 2029 being finalised, to be signed before year end
claims.note: Article 28 Oct: ironing out final details; both sides want to sign before the end of the calendar year; source Plettenberg.

claims.claim: No club or Kane confirmation of a signed deal in the sources
claims.note: The article quotes no statement from Bayern or Kane's camp.

claims.claim: Sky Sports, 16 Oct: agreed new deal in principle until summer 2029; paperwork being finalised; a few things to iron out
claims.note: Sky dated 16 Oct 2026; neither Kane nor Bayern confirmed in that article.

claims.claim: Kane confirmed talks in a report dated 29 August 2026 and said they were positive
claims.note: Bundesliga DE dated 29.08.2026: talks positive, so far so good; NST reports Kane confirming talks.

claims.claim: Kane quotes: first meeting started last week; no panic from either side; I'm sure both sides will be happy
claims.note: All three quotes verified word for word and attributed to Kane.

claims.claim: Signed from Tottenham in August 2023 on a four-year contract
claims.note: Al Jazeera (12 Aug 2023) and Sky (13 Aug 2023) both say four-year deal.

claims.claim: Sky: initial 86m pounds fee, add-ons taking it close to 100m, described as a Bayern and Bundesliga record
claims.note: Sky: initial 86m fee with add-ons close to 100m; record fee wording.

claims.claim: Al Jazeera: reported fee could top 100m pounds; highest fee ever paid by a Bundesliga club; previous record 80m euros Bayern paid for Lucas Hernandez in 2019
claims.note: Al Jazeera: reported fee could hit more than 100m pounds; highest fee for a Bundesliga club; previous record 80m euros from Atletico Madrid in 2019.

claims.claim: Tottenham 2019: 25 goals in 40 caps while he played for the club
claims.note: Spurs list reads 25 goals in 40 caps (2011-).

claims.claim: Jimmy Greaves' 266 goals for Spurs as the record Kane was chasing
claims.note: Spurs 8 June 2022 article cites Greaves' 266 at Spurs.

claims.claim: Lithuania debut March 2015; goal 79 seconds after coming off the bench
claims.note: Article: 79 seconds after coming off the bench against Lithuania, March 2015.

claims.claim: 99 caps, 66 goals and 17 assists before the 100th cap
claims.note: FA feature of 9 Sep 2024.

claims.claim: Hodgson 5 goals in 16 games; Southgate 61 in 81
claims.note: Matches FA figures.

claims.claim: 25 goals in 34 games at Wembley
claims.note: FA: a record 25 goals in 34 games at Wembley.

claims.claim: 17 goals in 14 World Cup qualifiers; 23 goals and 8 assists in 21 EURO qualifiers
claims.note: FA figures match.

claims.claim: Four against San Marino, first England player to do so since Ian Wright in November 1993
claims.note: FA: since Ian Wright in November 1993, also against San Marino.

claims.claim: March 2023 Italy goal passed Rooney's 53
claims.note: FA: breaking Rooney's record of 53 with a strike against Italy in March 2023.

claims.claim: Rooney's 53 goals came in 120 caps, 2003 to 2018
claims.note: Article: 53 goals in 120 caps between 2003 and 2018.

claims.claim: Nations League goal vs Germany made him the second England player to 50 goals, above Charlton's 49
claims.note: Article says exactly this.

claims.claim: Faced 44 countries; most often Italy (six) and Switzerland (five)
claims.note: FA figures match.

claims.claim: 15 major tournament goals from 29 appearances: 8 in 11 World Cup matches, 7 in 18 EURO finals matches
claims.note: FA figures match.

claims.claim: 14 World Cup goals; England's leading men's World Cup scorer ahead of Gary Lineker
claims.note: FA 2026 profile: moves him beyond Lineker.

claims.claim: Five England hat-tricks
claims.note: FA lists Panama, Bulgaria, Montenegro, Albania and San Marino.

claims.claim: Bulgaria treble took him to 25 international goals and above Geoff Hurst into the top 15
claims.note: Spurs 2019 article says this.

claims.claim: 2018 World Cup semi-finals and Golden Boot; four goals in three games at Euro 2020; England captain since 2017
claims.note: Article says all three.

claims.claim: Record caps as England captain, passing Bobby Moore; 125 senior caps, equalling Peter Shilton
claims.note: FA 2026 profile.

claims.claim: Bundesliga 2025/26: 36 goals, hat-trick in 5-1 win over Cologne; first player to win top scorer in each of first three seasons; Lewandowski only other three-in-a-row winner
claims.note: Bundesliga report dated 16 May 2026.

claims.claim: FA profile: 36 Bundesliga goals in 31 league games; 100 goals in 104 Bayern games; European Golden Shoe; third straight top scorer award; extraordinary scoring
claims.note: All figures match the FA profile.

claims.claim: Sky: Kane described as bookmakers' favourite before the ceremony; no odds quoted
claims.note: Sky: bookmakers' favourite; no odds or bookmaker named.

claims.claim: Accumulated voting points decide the prizes at the ceremony
claims.note: FA: accumulated points determine who takes the trophies.

claims.claim: England's record goalscorer
claims.note: FA records; passed Rooney in March 2023.

claims.claim: Kane is 33 as of 29 October 2026
claims.note: Date of birth 28 July 1993.

claims.claim: First ceremony held outside Paris
claims.note: FA profile: the ceremony is held outside Paris for the first time, in London.

valueNote: Adds the 28 October Magdeburg result with Kane rested, the Bundesliga vote details, the status of the tribute and the contract talks in one dated section, with the transfer fee given as reported by two outlets.
summary: Every claim checked matches its cited source. The fee and the contract status are attributed to the outlets that reported them.
